Revenue trend by channel   Month on x-axis; revenue as 2 lines: organic vs paid   Best top-level growth view   Organic revenue rises steadily from   $18.2k to $22.4k  ; paid is more volatile but ends higher than it started

Orders and revenue combo   Month on x-axis; bars for total orders, line for total revenue   Shows whether sales growth comes from more volume or bigger order value   Orders grow from   660 to 770   and revenue from   $32.8k to $41.3k  , indicating healthy volume-led growth

Paid efficiency chart   Month on x-axis; bars for paid ad spend, line for paid ROAS   Critical for ad budget control   Paid spend climbs from   $6.1k to $7.6k   while ROAS ranges roughly   2.22x–2.54x  , showing spend growth with only moderate efficiency gains
Month   Total Revenue   Total Orders   Organic AOV   Paid AOV   Paid ROAS
-   Organic is the growth engine.   Organic revenue increases every month, up about   23.1%   from January to April, with orders also rising steadily.
-   Paid has higher order value.   Paid AOV stays much higher than organic each month, ending at   $63.00   vs   $47.66   for organic.
-   Paid efficiency is uneven.   Ad spend keeps rising, but paid ROAS dips in March before recovering in April, so budget scaling should be monitored closely.
-   April is the strongest month.   It delivers the highest total revenue, highest total orders, and strongest organic performance.
-   Growth is mostly volume-driven, not price-driven.   Total orders rise meaningfully across the period, while AOV improves only modestly.
